blocks.en: Abstract
blocks.zh: 摘要

blocks.en: Instruction-following robots need navigation policies that reach high accuracy and remain inexpensive to train and to run on a single graphics processing unit (GPU). The most accurate vision-language navigation policies for continuous environments rely on language models with 4 to 8 billion parameters, long observation histories, and large auxiliary corpora. Two properties of the standard training setup limit smaller policies. Imitation labels cover the states that an expert visits, whereas the running policy reaches states that its own errors produce. In addition, an image-plane waypoint exists only while the route lies inside the camera view. We present \textbf{\paper}, a monocular red-green-blue (RGB) policy with 2 billion (2B) parameters that addresses both limitations. \paper adapts Qwen3-VL-2B with low-rank adapters and processes an eight-frame memory and the current view in one forward pass. The policy predicts the route direction as a bearing in the body frame of the agent, which remains defined for every heading, and a deterministic controller converts this bearing into motion. This design allows training to relabel the states that the policy itself visits. On-policy correction improves success, while bearing decoding outperforms image-plane waypoint scanning across all evaluated start headings with identical weights. On the \valunseen split, \paper achieves \rFinSR\% success on Room-to-Room in Continuous Environments (\rtor), averaged over three seeds, and \rRxFinSR\% on its Room-Across-Room counterpart (\rxr). Inference requires \rDecMs\,ms and \rInferGB\,GiB of memory, while training takes \rCostTrainTyp\ GPU-hours on one 12\,GB consumer GPU.

blocks.en:
Instruction-following navigation enables a robot to cross an unfamiliar building by following a route description.
Vision-and-language navigation in continuous environments (VLN-CE) formulates this task with low-level actions, namely 0.25 m forward steps, 15 ∘ 15^{\circ} turns, and a stop action [ 15 ] .
On the standard Room-to-Room in Continuous Environments (R2R-CE) benchmark, video-language models predict these actions from sequences of red-green-blue (RGB) observations.
NaVid [ 37 ] introduced this approach, Uni-NaVid [ 38 ] extended it to several navigation tasks, and NaVILA [ 8 ] and StreamVLN [ 34 ] scaled it further.
These systems are built on language models with 7B-8B parameters and long observation histories, and their training adds web video, question answering, or synthetic navigation episodes to the benchmark data.
StreamVLN and NaVILA report 270 and 595 ms per model call, respectively, on an RTX 4090 GPU, and training these 7B and 8B systems costs 544 to 2,816 data-center GPU-hours (details in Table 2 ).

blocks.en:
In an instruction-following setup, a deployed robot must act several times per second on its own hardware, so the latency, memory footprint, and training cost of its policy determine where that policy can run and who can afford to train it. Fig. 1 demonstrates AlphaNav among published systems along two axes, language-model size and latency.
It is visible that a 2B-parameter policy is on par in success rate with the 7B StreamVLN and the 8B NaVILA and Aux-Think at the lowest reported latency, whereas the 2B MonoDream [ 29 ] requires 800 ms per call and the 2B Goal2Pixel [ 3 ] needs depth at test time.
We identify two limitations of the standard training setup that stand in the way of compact policies.
The first concerns the training data, since imitation covers only the states an expert visits, whereas a running policy drifts into new states after its own errors [ 25 ] . The second concerns the action representation, because an image-plane waypoint can express only routes inside the camera view, yet in 54.5% of the Val-Unseen episodes the first route step lies more than 90 ∘ 90^{\circ} from the start heading.

blocks.en:
AlphaNav retains a standard vision-language backbone and instead changes the output representation and the training-state distribution (Fig. 2 ).
The instruction, eight memory frames, and the current frame form one sequence with 192 visual tokens for Qwen3-VL-2B [ 2 ] , which we fine-tune with low-rank adaptation (LoRA) [ 11 ] .
A feature-wise linear modulation (FiLM) layer [ 21 ] conditions the current-view tokens on known camera and body parameters.
Four heads then predict a waypoint heatmap, a visibility score, a stop probability, and a 24-bin route bearing, which encodes the direction of the route in the body frame and remains defined for every heading.
A deterministic controller converts these predictions into turns and at most four forward moves.
Training first imitates reference paths and then relabels the states of the policy’s own rollouts in rounds of on-policy correction (Secs. 3.5 and S11 ). The core contributions of AlphaNav are as follows: 1. We present AlphaNav, a compact monocular policy that adapts Qwen3-VL-2B with LoRA and processes eight memory frames and the current view in one forward pass.
Over three seeds, AlphaNav reaches 53.3 ± \pm 1.4% success rate (SR) and 49.3% success weighted by path length (SPL) on R2R-CE Val-Unseen. 2. We train the policy on the states that it visits, and this relabeling raises SR from 43.9% to 49.3%.
With oracle inputs the controller succeeds in 99.7% of the episodes, and an oracle stop raises the SR of one trained model from 53.6% to 72.5%. 3. We pair the image-plane waypoint with a 24-bin body-frame route-bearing head that remains defined for every heading, and we isolate its effect by decoding the same weights both ways.
The bearing raises SR from 39.7% to 53.6%, and on the baseline recipe the orient-then-go augmentation adds 4.6 points on starts that face away from the route. 4. AlphaNav has the lowest latency of the ten compared systems that report one and trains on one consumer GPU.
One decision requires 65 ms and 4.3 GiB of memory, and training requires 30.6 GPU-hours plus 11.2 GPU-hours of label rendering on one RTX 5070; training alone takes 18 to 92 times fewer GPU-hours than the 7B and 8B systems report.

blocks.en: 2 Related Work
blocks.zh: 2 相关工作

blocks.en:
VLN-CE [ 15 ] extends Room-to-Room (R2R) [ 1 ] to continuous navigation with low-level actions; Room-Across-Room (RxR) [ 17 ] provides longer instructions, while EnvDrop [ 27 ] uses back-translation.
Depth supports several planning representations: semantic maps in CM2 and WS-MGMap [ 9 , 7 ] , language-aligned waypoints in LAW [ 23 ] , and panoramic topological graphs in ETP-R1 and LCGNav [ 36 , 20 ] .
Other depth-based methods construct 3D feature fields [ 32 , 32 ] or provide VLMs with annotated maps and layered 3D tokens [ 40 , 33 ] .
Zero-shot planners prompt large language models with constraint-aware or affordance-oriented plans [ 6 , 5 ] , generic instructions [ 18 ] , or predicted trajectories [ 30 ] .
RGB-only policies remove depth dependence: NaVid and Uni-NaVid predict actions from RGB histories [ 37 , 38 ] , while NaVILA and StreamVLN use 8B and 7B backbones [ 8 , 34 ] .
Aux-Think examines reasoning strategies for data-efficient training [ 28 ] , while DualVLN and InternVLA-N1 combine slow planners with fast low-level policies [ 33 , 13 ] .
Efficiency is pursued through 2B backbones in VLN-R1 and MonoDream [ 22 , 29 ] , reduced training cost in Efficient-VLN [ 41 ] , and geometry-aware bird’s-eye representations in GA-VLN [ 35 ] .
MemVLN addresses memory cost by compressing history into 300 tokens within a 4B model [ 31 ] .
However, some 2B policies require test-time depth [ 3 ] , incur higher latency [ 29 ] , or achieve lower success [ 22 ] , motivating closer attention to training and output design.

VLN-CE [15] 将"室-对室"(R2R)[1]扩展为以低等动作进行连续导航;"室-跨室"(RxR)[17]提供更长的指示,而"EnvDrop [27]使用回译.
深度支持一些规划表述:CM2和WS-MGMap [9,7]中的语义图,LAW中语言相通的路由点 [23];ETP-R1和LCGNav中全景地貌图 [36,20].
其他以深度为基础的方法构建了3D特征字段[32,32],或提供了VLM有注释的地图和分层的3D符号[40,33].
零射线规划者会促使大型语言模型具有约束意识或以支付能力为导向的计划[6,5],通用指令[18],或预测出轨迹[30].
仅RGB政策消除了深度依赖:NaVid和Uni-NaVid从RGB历史中预测动作[37,38],而NaVILA和StreamVLN则使用8B和7B骨干[8,34].
Aux-Think审查数据高效培训的推理策略 [28],而DualVLN和InternVLA-N1将慢规划者与快低级政策结合[33,13].
通过VLN-R1和MonoDream的2B骨干追求效率,降低高效-VLN[41]的训练费用,以及GA-VLN[35]的几何-认知鸟眼表现.
MemVLN通过将历史压缩为4B型 [31] 内300个符来解决内存成本.
然而,一些2B政策需要测试时间深度[3],需要更高的延迟度[29],或取得更低的成功[22],这促使人们更加关注培训和产出设计。

blocks.en:
Beyond model size, training must account for the states encountered during deployment. DAgger addresses the distribution shift of behavior cloning by collecting labels for states encountered by the learner [ 25 ] .
Efficient-VLN uses within-episode correction [ 41 ] , while JOP-VLN and ETP-R1 additionally apply GRPO [ 10 , 36 ] .
Output representations determine target availability: panoramic models predict polar waypoints from 12-view RGB-D observations [ 16 , 11 ] , covering every heading.
Goal2Pixel lifts image-plane goals using depth [ 3 ] , while Qwen-RobotNav predicts robot-centric waypoints that remain defined outside the camera view [ 39 ] .
With one camera, however, image-plane waypoints require a visible route point and cannot supervise routes behind the agent, whether initially or after a wrong turn.
Camera-robust policies canonicalize geometry across platforms [ 14 , 24 ] or enforce cross-view action consistency [ 12 ] .
Augmentation additionally requires consistency between transformed observations, directional instructions, and supervision.
For mirroring, this includes swapping left/right words in instructions. Within a single 2B RGB policy, AlphaNav conditions on camera parameters, applies only augmentations that preserve exact labels, and represents eight raw 128 × 128 128\times 128 history frames with 128 tokens.
blocks.zh:
除了模型规模之外,培训还必须考虑到部署期间遇到的州。 Dagger通过收集学习者遇到的状态的标签来解决行为克隆的分布转移[25].
高效的VLN在系统内部使用校正[41],而JOP-VLN和ETP-R1则额外应用了GRPO[10,36].
输出表示决定了目标可用性:全景模型预测从12视图RGB-D观测中得出的极地出行点[16,11],涵盖每个标题.
Goal2Pixel使用深度[3]提升图像-平面目标,而Quen-RobotNav则预测出在相机视图外仍然被定义的以机器人为中心的方式点 [39].
然而,用一台相机,图像-平面航道点需要一个可见的路由点,并且无论是最初还是错误转弯后,都无法监督代理后行道.
相机-robust政策能将相机跨平台几何化[14,24]或执行交叉视图动作一致性[12].
增强还需要转变的观测、方向指示和监督之间保持一致。
对于镜像,这包括将指令中的左/右字互换. 在单一的2B RGB政策内,相机参数上的AlphaNav条件,只应用保留准确标签的增强功能,并代表了8个生128×128128\times128历史帧和128个符.

blocks.en: 3.2 Route bearing in the body frame

blocks.en:
An image-plane waypoint, the pixel 𝒖 t \bm{u}_{t} of the next route point, gives the direction θ t pix = arctan ⁡ ( ( c x − u t , x ) / f x ) \theta^{\mathrm{pix}}_{t}=\arctan\!\big((c_{x}-u_{t,x})/f_{x}\big) , with the horizontal focal length f x f_{x} and principal-point coordinate c x c_{x} , only while that point lies inside the field of view.
When the route is beside or behind the agent, either at the start of an episode or after a wrong turn, the waypoint policy must turn to locate it. However, these states lack waypoint labels during training. AlphaNav therefore also predicts the route bearing, the direction of the route target in the body frame of the agent. For a target at body coordinates ( x t , y t ) (x_{t},y_{t}) , with x x forward and y y to the left, the bearing label θ t ⋆ = atan2 ⁡ ( y t , x t ) \theta^{\star}_{t}=\operatorname{atan2}(y_{t},x_{t}) is defined at every heading and at every position farther than 0.3 m from the target.
The policy predicts the bearing as a distribution 𝒑 t \bm{p}_{t} over N = 24 N=24 circular bins with centers θ k = − π + 2 ​ π ​ k / N \theta_{k}=-\pi+2\pi k/N , one bin per 15 ∘ 15^{\circ} turn primitive, and the predicted bearing θ ^ t \hat{\theta}_{t} is the probability-weighted circular mean of the most likely bin and its two neighbors.
At inference, the controller can therefore turn directly toward a route that is out of view, and it keeps the waypoint as the finer target while the route is in view. In training, the direction label exists at every heading, including at off-route states whose target lies out of view and which therefore lack an image-plane label.
On-policy relabeling can thus supervise the output on which the controller acts at all of these states.

blocks.en: 3.3 Architecture
blocks.zh: 3.3 建筑

blocks.en:
We adapt Qwen3-VL-2B-Instruct [ 2 ] with LoRA adapters [ 11 ] on its language decoder and vision tower, and train only these adapters, the camera conditioning, and the heads.
One sequence holds the instruction, the K = 8 K=8 memory frames in temporal order ( 128 × 128 128\times 128 pixels, 16 tokens each), and the current frame (64 tokens), so every current-view token attends to the instruction and to the whole memory in one forward pass.
At inference, a new frame is appended to the memory only once the agent has moved 0.5 m since the last appended frame, and otherwise it replaces the newest entry, so that turning in place does not push earlier spatial context out of the memory.
A FiLM layer [ 21 ] , initialized as the identity, scales and shifts each current-view feature 𝒛 t , j \bm{z}_{t,j} of the final decoder layer with parameters predicted from 𝜿 ∈ ℝ 8 \bm{\kappa}\in\mathbb{R}^{8} , which gives 𝒛 ^ t , j \hat{\bm{z}}_{t,j} .
The vector 𝜿 \bm{\kappa} holds the logarithms of the focal lengths, the relative principal point, the camera height and pitch, and the robot width and turning radius, so that the mapping from image positions to directions can follow the camera.
The memory reaches these features through decoder attention, so the heads read only current-view features.

blocks.zh: 3.4 主计长

blocks.en:
The controller 𝒞 \mathcal{C} follows one principle: it moves far only when the route is in view and ahead, and otherwise it turns toward the predicted bearing and observes again. Stop is issued when the stop probability exceeds a threshold, after ln ⁡ w \ln w is subtracted from the logit to remove the shift that the class weight w w of the stop loss introduces (Sec. S8 ). Commit applies when the route is predicted visible within a cone ahead: the agent turns toward 𝒖 t \bm{u}_{t} and moves 1 m, so one forward pass covers four primitives. Reorient applies otherwise: the agent turns toward θ ^ t \hat{\theta}_{t} and observes again, or moves 0.5 m if it already faces a route that is predicted out of view (the hidden-route rule).
A turn-loop guard adds two forward moves after a run of turn-only decisions.
The image-plane readout commits whenever the route is predicted visible, and because θ t pix \theta^{\mathrm{pix}}_{t} cannot point outside the view, it scans instead of reorienting: it turns 90 ∘ 90^{\circ} in place and observes again.
Table 20 lists the thresholds, and Sec. S6 reports how often each rule acts.

blocks.en:
Stage 1 imitates the reference routes of R2R-CE, English Room-Across-Room in Continuous Environments (RxR-CE), and EnvDrop [ 27 ] in training houses only, with randomized appearance and cameras.
Mirroring reflects the frames and spatial labels and swaps “left” and “right”, which keeps the labels exact for a centered principal point.
Orient-then-go draws a uniform start heading and prepends a turning clause such as “Turn around.”, which adds starts whose route is out of view.
Imitation covers states near the reference routes, whereas the running policy also reaches states that its own errors produce.
Stage 2 therefore follows DAgger [ 25 ] : the policy drives rollouts on R2R-CE training episodes, every visited state is relabeled from the live pose with the rule above, and the relabeled states are aggregated with the original data.
For an off-route state, the progress along the reference route advances to the nearest route point within a short window ahead, and the target is chosen from there, so the label leads back to the instructed route rather than along a new shortest path to the goal.
Because the bearing label exists at every heading, the correction also covers states whose route is out of view.
As in Efficient-VLN [ 41 ] , the policy controls decision i i of L L expected decisions with probability 0.6 min ⁡ ( 1 , i / ( L − 1 ) ) 0.6^{\min(1,\,i/(L-1))} , and the oracle briefly takes over when the agent strays from the path or is blocked.
Stage 1 trains for 10,000 steps on 57,513 episodes, stage 2 runs three rounds of 1,500 rollouts each, and the trained parameters amount to 75.8 M of 2203 M.
Sec. S11 and Table 20 give the data, the optimization, and the controller thresholds, and Sec. S11 the round-level schedule that serves as an ablation baseline.

We evaluate on R2R-CE [ 15 ] , which ports Room-to-Room [ 1 ] on Matterport3D [ 4 ] to the Habitat simulator [ 26 ] .
Unless stated otherwise, all results refer to the Val-Unseen split, which contains 1,839 episodes in 11 buildings that do not appear in training.
The Val-Seen split, in contrast, contains 778 episodes in the training buildings.
We select checkpoints on 100 and the inference settings on 300 of these episodes before evaluating AlphaNav on Val-Unseen (Sec. S10 ).
At each step, the agent observes a 256 × 256 256\times 256 RGB frame with a 90 ∘ 90^{\circ} horizontal field of view, captured from a height of 1.25 m.
The benchmark limits each episode to 500 primitive actions (see Sec. S10 for the full protocol).
An episode counts as successful if the agent stops within 3 m of the goal.
Accordingly, we report the success rate (SR), the success weighted by path length (SPL), the oracle success rate (OSR), and the navigation error (NE) in meters.
We train AlphaNav with three seeds and each ablation model with a single seed.
The only exception is the on-policy schedule, which we replicate on all three seeds (Sec. 4.3 ).
Values in brackets are 95% bootstrap intervals over buildings, differences between models are paired over episodes, and all differences and means are computed before rounding.
Finally, we measure latency and memory at batch size 1 on a single 12 GB RTX 5070, the same GPU we use for training (Sec. S10 ).

blocks.en:
Using only a single RGB camera, AlphaNav (Table 1 ) matches or exceeds the SR of every map-based, zero-shot (Table 7 ), and 3D-feature-field method.
The only exceptions are InternVLA-N1 and GA-VLN, which both rely on depth input and 7B language models.
Among RGB video-language policies, AlphaNav (53.3% SR, 49.3% SPL) is on par with the 7B StreamVLN (52.8% and 47.2%) and the 8B NaVILA (54.0% and 49.0%) and Aux-Think (54.8% and 46.9%) with less than a third of their parameters, and it trains only on R2R-CE, RxR-CE [ 17 ] , and EnvDrop [ 27 ] .
The 4B MemVLN reaches 55.0% SR with R2R-CE and RxR-CE alone.
AlphaNav outperforms NaVid and Uni-NaVid by 15.9 and 6.3 SR points, respectively, and the 2B VLN-R1 by 27.7 points. Among the other 2B systems, AlphaNav is on par with MonoDream (2.5 SR points lower, SPL 49.3% vs. 49.1%) at 12 times lower latency, and with Goal2Pixel (0.8 points lower), which requires depth at test time and runs at 1.8 times the latency.
Both SRs lie inside the 95% interval [47.1, 58.8] of our mean over the 11 Val-Unseen buildings.
The strongest RGB systems, Efficient-VLN, DualVLN, Qwen-RobotNav, and JOP-VLN, reach 61% to 73% SR, but they rely on larger backbones, more training data, or reinforcement learning.
The published results are single runs, whereas we report the mean over three seeds, which reach 53.6, 51.8, and 54.5% SR; the best reaches 50.8% SPL. To quantify the effect of our training recipe, we compare AlphaNav with a baseline recipe.
This earlier configuration trains on R2R-CE alone for 4,000 steps, omits the two augmentations, runs only one round of the round-level on-policy schedule (Sec. S11 ), and stops at a threshold of 0.6.
In a paired comparison on all 1,839 episodes, AlphaNav gains + 13.9 +13.9 [ + 8.7 +8.7 , + 17.5 +17.5 ] points over this baseline (from 39.4% to 53.3%).
The gain is positive in every third of the route lengths, with + 7.8 +7.8 , + 16.9 +16.9 , and + 16.8 +16.8 points from the shortest to the longest third, and in 9 of the 11 Val-Unseen buildings (Fig. 5 ).

blocks.en: 4.2 Accuracy and cost
blocks.zh: 4.2 准确性和费用

blocks.en:
Table 2 lists the inference and training costs as reported by each paper.
AlphaNav uses 192 visual tokens and 75.8 M trainable parameters, and one decision takes 65 ms, of which the forward pass accounts for 64 ms.
In closed loop, which additionally includes the controller, the simulator, and rendering, a decision takes 85.7 ms (Sec. S6 ).
In terms of memory, AlphaNav peaks at 4.3 GiB, compared with 18.5 GB for NaVILA at 16-bit precision and 20 GB for DualVLN.
Its latency is the lowest among the ten systems that report one.
Specifically, it is 1.8 times lower than that of Goal2Pixel, the next fastest system, and 4, 9, and 12 times lower than those of StreamVLN, NaVILA, and MonoDream.
These three systems were measured on an RTX 4090, a faster GPU with 1.5 times the memory bandwidth of our RTX 5070.
Because some systems execute several primitives per call, we also normalize the latency by the number of executed primitives.
Per primitive, AlphaNav requires 17.9 ms, compared with 68, 50, and 40 ms for StreamVLN, Uni-NaVid, and Efficient-VLN v2, which each predict four actions per call.
To compare the systems independently of the GPU, we further estimate the compute per decision.
One decision of AlphaNav processes 241 tokens on average and requires an estimated 1.31 tera floating-point operations (TFLOPs), compared with 8.73 TFLOPs per call reported for GA-VLN (Table 11 ).
Training is similarly inexpensive.
It requires 30.6 GPU-hours on one RTX 5070 with a peak memory of 7.9 GiB, plus 11.2 GPU-hours for rendering the labels.
Training alone thus takes 18 to 92 times fewer GPU-hours (13 to 67 times with rendering) than the 544 to 2,816 data-center GPU-hours reported by the 7B and 8B systems in Table 2 that state their training cost.
The labels are rendered once and shared by the three seeds.
At 65 ms per decision, the policy runs at 15 decisions per second, above the 10 calls per second marked in Fig. 1 .

blocks.en: 4.3 On-policy data and the controller ceiling
blocks.zh: 4.3 (中文(简体) ). 政策数据和控制器上限

blocks.en:
Training on the states that the policy itself visits yields clear gains over the imitation stage (Table 3 a, Figs. 6 and 11 ).
SR rises from 43.9% after imitation to 47.1% when the policy drives 47.3% of the rollout steps (round-level schedule), and to 49.3% ( + 5.4 +5.4 [ + 2.1 +2.1 , + 8.2 +8.2 ] points) when it drives 65.0% (within-episode schedule).
The within-episode schedule thus gains + 2.2 +2.2 [ + 0.7 +0.7 , + 3.7 +3.7 ] points over the round-level schedule, which also uses fewer rollouts per round (1,000 against 1,500).
The gain over imitation replicates on the other two seeds, with + 5.8 +5.8 [ + 3.9 +3.9 , + 8.2 +8.2 ] and + 3.5 +3.5 [ + 1.1 +1.1 , + 5.3 +5.3 ] points (Table 5 ).
On top of this, the inference settings selected on Val-Seen add + 4.2 +4.2 [ + 1.6 +1.6 , + 7.2 +7.2 ] points (row 4 against row 3); averaged over the three seeds, the memory spacing contributes + 3.3 +3.3 points and the stop threshold + 0.9 +0.9 points (Table 15 , Sec. S8 ).
To separate the effect of on-policy training from that of the inference settings, we also compare both stages at equal settings on 300 Val-Seen episodes, where on-policy training raises the SR of seed 42 from 49.0% to 62.7% ( + 13.7 +13.7 [ + 9.2 +9.2 , + 17.8 +17.8 ] points).

blocks.en:
To measure how much error stems from the controller, we execute oracle route bearings and stop once within 1.5 m of the goal; this controller ceiling succeeds in 99.7% of the Val-Unseen episodes.
The remaining failures therefore lie mainly in the policy’s predictions, and most of them are stops far from the goal.
In particular, seed 42 stops more than 5 m from the goal in 32.9% of episodes, which accounts for 71% of its failures.
Replacing only the learned stop with an oracle stop within 1.5 m of the goal raises the SR of the same navigation from 53.6% to 72.5% ( + 18.9 +18.9 [ + 16.4 +16.4 , + 22.1 +22.1 ] points), which recovers 41% of the failures of this seed.
The stop head itself ranks decisions well, with an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC) of 0.89.
In addition, SR stays between 51.6% and 53.3% for every threshold from 0.6 to 0.9 (Table 15 ).
The headroom therefore lies not in the threshold but in where the policy stops: over three seeds, 34.0% of episodes stop without any decision within 3 m of the goal, and 8.9% pass within 3 m of the goal but still fail.
Finally, success depends on the memory: on 300 selection episodes with seed 42, keeping only four of the eight memory frames at inference lowers SR from 62.7% to 18.0%, and without any memory frames, no episode stops at all (Sec. S8 ).

因此,剩下的失败主要在于政策的预测,其中大部分都远远没有达到目标。
特别是,42号种子在32.9%的赛事中与入球相距超过5米,占出局失败的71%.
仅用在入球1.5米以内的甲骨文站取而代之,将同一导航的SR从53.6%提升到72.5%(+18.9+18.9 [+16.4+16.4,+22.1+22.1]分),恢复了这颗种子失败的41%.

blocks.en: 4.4 Route-bearing output and augmentations

blocks.en:
To isolate the effect of the output interface, we decode one set of weights in two ways (readouts, Table 3 b).
Both readouts share the training data, the seed, and every weight, so their difference stems from the readout and its turning rule; the on-policy rounds of these weights ran the bearing readout.
Both readouts steer to the waypoint when they commit, and the bearing readout commits only when its decoded bearing also lies within the cone.
Toward a route that is out of view, the route bearing turns directly to the predicted direction, whereas the scan turns 90 ∘ 90^{\circ} in place and observes again (Sec. 3.4 ).
Decoded as a route bearing, the same weights raise SR from 39.7% to 53.6% ( + 13.9 +13.9 [ + 8.5 +8.5 , + 19.3 +19.3 ] points).
The bearing leads in all four start-heading bins, by + 15.5 +15.5 points on starts within 90 ∘ 90^{\circ} of the route and by + 12.5 +12.5 points on starts beyond 90 ∘ 90^{\circ} (Fig. 4(a) and Sec. S4 ).
The gain is even larger on starts that face the route because the route also leaves the view later in the episode: only 46.9% of all decisions commit toward a visible route.
On starts beyond 90 ∘ 90^{\circ} , its first turn faces the route in 69.0% of the cases, against 50.3% for the scan, and in 65.5% and 67.8% for seeds 43 and 44 (Table 6 ).
On the baseline recipe, the orient-then-go augmentation, which targets starts that face away from the route, adds + 4.6 +4.6 [ + 1.2 +1.2 , + 8.7 +8.7 ] points on starts beyond 90 ∘ 90^{\circ} , + 2.3 +2.3 points on the remaining starts, and + 3.5 +3.5 [ + 1.1 +1.1 , + 6.0 +6.0 ] points over all starts (Fig. 4(b) , Table 3 c).
Fig. 3 shows four successes of AlphaNav (seed 42), each with an SPL of 1.00, and one failure in which the agent passes close to the goal but its stop probability peaks at 0.82, below the threshold of 0.9 (more episodes in Sec. S2 ).

blocks.en: 4.5 Results on RxR-CE
blocks.zh: 4.5 关于RxR-CE的结果

blocks.en:
To test whether our findings carry over to longer and more varied instructions, we evaluate the same three models on the 3,669 English episodes of RxR-CE Val-Unseen [ 17 , 15 ] .
We tune no setting on RxR-CE, and its English training episodes enter imitation only.
On this benchmark, AlphaNav reaches 40.8 ± \pm 1.4% SR [36.9, 44.6] and 36.4% SPL (Table 4 ).
This places it 19.4 points above VLN-R1 and 1.9 and 8.6 points below Goal2Pixel and MonoDream, respectively, as reported by these papers (see Table 9 for larger systems).
The gain of the route-bearing output also replicates on RxR-CE.
On the weights of seed 42, it raises SR from 27.3% with the scan readout to 41.2% ( + 13.9 +13.9 [ + 11.2 +11.2 , + 15.8 +15.8 ] points), the same gain as on R2R-CE (Sec. 4.4 ).
Likewise, the imitation-only stage of this seed reaches 36.2% SR at its own inference settings, + 5.0 +5.0 [ + 0.3 +0.3 , + 8.1 +8.1 ] points below the final model.
Finally, SR counts the 99 episodes (2.7%) whose goal is unreachable on our navigation mesh as failures.
Excluding these episodes, SR is 41.9%.

我们不调RxR-CE的设置,其英语训练节目只录入模仿.
在这个基准上, AlphaNav达到40.8±\pm 1.4% SR [36.9, 44.6]和36.4% SPL(表4).

在种子42的权重上,将SR从扫描读出后27.3%提升到41.2%(+13.9+13.9 [+11.2+11.2,+15.8+15.8]分]),与R2R-CE(sec 4.4)上的增益相同.

不包括这些事件,斯洛伐克共和国为41.9%。

blocks.en: 5 Conclusion and Limitations
blocks.zh: 5. 结论和限制

blocks.en:
We presented AlphaNav, a compact monocular VLN-CE policy that predicts the route as a body-frame bearing and trains on the states that it visits.
With one RGB camera and a 2B model, AlphaNav reaches 53.3 ± \pm 1.4% SR and 49.3% SPL on R2R-CE over three seeds and 40.8% SR on English RxR-CE.
Each decision requires 65 ms and 4.3 GiB of memory, and training requires 30.6 GPU-hours on one 12 GB consumer GPU.
On-policy training raises SR from 43.9% to 49.3%, with gains on all three seeds.
The route bearing raises the SR of the same weights from 39.7% to 53.6% over an image-plane waypoint, in every start-heading bin, with the same gain on RxR-CE.
With oracle inputs, the controller succeeds in 99.7% of episodes, and an oracle stop raises SR from 53.6% to 72.5%, which recovers 41% of the failures.
blocks.zh:
我们提出了AlphaNav, 一个紧凑的单一VLN-CE政策, 预测路线是一个车体框架,
有一台RGB相机和一台2B型相机,AlphaNav在3个种子上达到53.3±\pm 1.4%的SR和49.3%的SPL在R2R-CE上达到40.8%的SR在英国RxR-CE上达到.
每个决定都需要65 ms和4.3 GiB的内存,培训需要30.6 GPU小时1个GB消费GPU.
政策性培训将SR从43.9%提高到49.3%,所有三种种子都有收获.
航道轴承将相同重量的SR从39.7%提升到53.6%,在每架起航站楼的起航道点,RxR-CE的起航道点上,其收益也相同.
使用甲骨文输入,控制器在99.7%的发作中成功,甲骨文停止将SR从53.6%提升到72.5%,恢复了41%的故障.

blocks.en:
Limitations and Future work: Our evaluation follows the standard simulated benchmarks, R2R-CE and the English subset of RxR-CE, with one 2B backbone and cameras near the training range (Sec. S7 ).
Extending the study to further backbones, to the other languages of RxR-CE, and to wider cameras is left to future work.
Future work will also improve the stop decision, behind 41% of the failures, and test the policy on a physical robot.

将研究扩展到进一步的骨干,RxR-CE的其他语言,以及更宽的相机,则留待未来工作.
未来的工作也会改善停站决定,41%的故障背后,并测试物理机器人的政策.

blocks.en:
The bin count matches the turn primitive of the benchmark, and the decoding window leaves every logged action unchanged.
Every model uses 24 bins of 15 ∘ 15^{\circ} , one bin per turn primitive, and a decoded bearing therefore turns the agent by whole primitives (Sec. 3.4 ).
Positive angles point left, bin N / 2 N/2 points forward, and bin 0 points backward.
A circular mean over the most likely bin and at most its two neighbors stays within half a bin ( 7.5 ∘ 7.5^{\circ} ) of the center of that bin, because the center carries the largest weight.
The two-bin and three-bin means therefore produce the same number of 15 ∘ 15^{\circ} turns as the most likely bin alone.
The decoding window can change the controller output only through the 40 ∘ 40^{\circ} cone of the four-move commit, namely when the policy predicts a visible route and the most likely bin is centered at ± 45 ∘ \pm 45^{\circ} .
On unseen buildings, this condition holds for 0.9% of the non-stop decisions of the three seeds.
The three-bin mean moves none of these decisions inside the cone (0.0%), which confirms that decoding the most likely bin alone produces the same action at every logged decision.
In the open-loop test of Fig. 17 , the center of the most likely bin lies on average 12.9 ∘ from the target bearing at the training field of view, which is less than one bin width.

blocks.en: S5 Label-preserving augmentations
blocks.zh: S5 保有标签的增强

blocks.en:
The two augmentations of Sec. S11 keep their labels exact under the following conditions.
The mirror augmentation requires a principal point on the center column, which holds for every generated frame.
It also requires a swap of every directional left and right word, while compass words and the adverbial use of “left” or “right”, as in “stop right before the door”, keep their form.
In addition, the swap must act as an involution, meaning that a second application restores the original instruction.
An automated check over the 57,513 training instructions, taken as the model receives them, finds a directional word in 50,496 instructions (87.8%).
Applying the swap twice restores 50,495 of these exactly and leaves the remaining instructions identical.
The one exception is an RxR-CE instruction that contains the spelling “leFt”, which returns with a lower-case “f”.
The orient-then-go augmentation applies to episodes with a uniformly drawn start heading and inserts its clause only when the required rotation is at least 45 ∘ 45^{\circ} .
blocks.zh:
Sec. S11的两次增强在以下条件下保持其标签精确.
镜面放大需要中心柱上有一个主点,每个生成的相框都持有.
它还要求将每一个左右方向的词相换,而罗盘词和 " 左 " 或 " 右 " 的旁接用法,如 " 在门前站住 " ,保留其形式。
此外,互换必须起到进取作用,即第二个应用程序恢复了原指令.
对57,513项训练指示进行自动检查,如模型收到这些指示,在50,496项指示(87.8%)中找到方向字。
两次应用互换可以完全恢复其中的50,495个,其余的指令保持不变.
一个例外是含有拼写"leFt"的RxR-CE指令,它以小写"f"返回.
Orient-when-go 增强适用于一个统一划出起步标题的相片,并且只有在要求的旋转至少为45~~45~~circ}时才插入其条款.

blocks.en:
The instruction sensitivity measures how often the first turn follows the direction words of the instruction.
It is the share of first turns that flip when we swap the left and right words of the first clause while the scene stays unchanged, measured on the episodes with a directional word in that clause.
The baseline recipe flips 0.44 of its first turns, and the orient-then-go model flips 0.21.
On these 389 episodes, the swap lowers SR by 8.5 points for the baseline recipe and by 4.1 points for the orient-then-go model, so the direction words change both the first turn and the outcome.

blocks.en:
We evaluate the three seeds of AlphaNav in Table 1 on the 3,669 English guide episodes of RxR-CE Val-Unseen [ 17 , 15 ] .
English is the language of the training instructions (en-US and en-IN; 96 words per instruction on average), and we do not evaluate the Hindi and Telugu episodes.
The settings are those selected on R2R-CE Val-Seen, without any change or tuning on RxR-CE.
English RxR-CE training episodes are part of the imitation data (Sec. S11 ), and the on-policy rounds use R2R-CE alone.
They comprise a 90 ∘ 90^{\circ} field of view, 500 primitives per episode, and success within 3 m by geodesic distance.
We evaluate each seed once, and AlphaNav reaches 40.8 ± \pm 1.4% SR (interval [36.9, 44.6]) and 36.4% SPL (Table 10 ).
This SR lies 12.5 points below its SR on R2R-CE.
Among the 2B systems with published RxR-CE results (Table 9 ), it lies 19.4 points above VLN-R1 (21.4%) and 1.9 and 8.6 points below Goal2Pixel (42.7%) and MonoDream (49.4%).
By locale, SR is 44.7% on the 1,223 en-US episodes and 38.9% on the 2,446 en-IN episodes.
The imitation-only model of seed 42 (stage 1) reaches 36.2% SR, and the final model lies + 5.0 +5.0 points above it (interval + 0.3 +0.3 to + 8.1 +8.1 ).
Because the two runs use different inference rules, with stop threshold 0.7 and no memory spacing for the imitation-only model and stop threshold 0.9 and 0.5 m spacing for the final model, this gain combines the effects of on-policy training and the inference rule.
The weights and the rule of seed 42 also decode with the image-plane readout that scans in place, which reaches 27.3% SR and 23.1% SPL.
The route bearing therefore exceeds the scan by + 13.9 +13.9 [ + 11.2 +11.2 , + 15.8 +15.8 ] points on RxR-CE, compared with + 13.9 +13.9 points on R2R-CE.
The instructions average 109 tokens, so a decision processes 319 tokens on average, compared with 241 on R2R-CE.
At the median English instruction, a decision takes 83 ms and 4.4 GiB, measured as in Sec. S10 , and the closed loop takes 95 ms per decision over 43.9 decisions per episode on average.
In every run, 99 episodes (2.7%) in one building have a goal that is unreachable on our navigation mesh.
SR, OSR, and SPL count these episodes as not reached, and NE averages the other episodes, on which the SR is 41.9%.
We compute normalized dynamic time warping (nDTW), which measures how closely the path follows the reference path, as in VLN-CE, and we reconstruct the path per move from the decision-level positions.
None of the compared papers states which language subset its RxR-CE table covers, and we list their values as reported.

The closed-loop cost depends on how many decisions an episode takes and on how far each decision moves the agent.
Over the three seeds on unseen buildings, an episode takes 25.8 decisions on average, with a median of 16.
A decision executes 3.65 policy primitives on average, which amounts to 17.9 ms of isolated decision time per executed primitive.
Including the controller, simulator steps, and rendering, the loop takes 85.7 ms per decision, measured over the 141,907 decisions of the episodes that stay in the building of the previous episode.
A decision moves the agent 0.45 m horizontally on average and at most 1.05 m, and 37% of the decisions leave its position unchanged.
At 1 m/s, the mean motion takes 6.9 times the isolated decision latency and 5.3 times the closed-loop time per decision.

blocks.en:
The controller cases show how often each controller rule acts and how often its forward moves collide.
Of the 142,458 policy decisions of the three seeds, 46.9% commit four moves toward a route that is predicted visible within the 40 ∘ 40^{\circ} cone, and 28.9% only turn.
In addition, 15.2% take two moves because the agent already faces a route that is predicted out of view (the hidden-route rule), 5.2% consist of moves of the turn-loop guard, and 3.7% stop.
The commits account for 82.7% of all forward moves, with one forward pass each.
Of the commits, 81.4% execute all four moves, and a collision ends the others.
Of the commit moves, 94.5% are collision-free.
A forward move collides in 5.5% of the commit moves, compared with 23.2% of the moves of the hidden-route rule and 19.5% of the guard moves.
The controller takes both of these shorter move types when no visible route lies within the cone.
The long commit therefore occurs where the route is in view, and the short steps occur where the route is out of view.
In 12.9% of all forward moves, the agent travels less than 0.23 m because it slides along an obstacle, and the next decision processes a new frame at most 1.05 m later.
With oracle route bearings and an oracle stop within 1.5 m, the same commits reach 99.7% SR (Sec. 4.3 ).
On the 300 selection episodes of the inference batch, with seed 42, stop threshold 0.7, and every frame appended, the hidden-route rule reaches 58.7% SR with two moves and 57.7% with one move.
blocks.zh:

在三个种子的142 458项政策决定中,46.9%的种子向40分之40的圆锥内预想可见的路线投放了4道,28.9%只转弯.
此外,15.2%的人采取两起动作,因为代理人已经面临一个被预言出局的路线(隐藏路线规则),5.2%由转弯后卫的动作组成,3.7%的停站.
承付款占所有前行的82.7%,每行一次。
在承诺中,81.4%执行全部4个动作,相撞结束其他动作.
在承诺的动作中,94.5%是无相撞的.
前行相撞占承诺动作的5.5%,而后行相撞占隐藏行道规则动作的23.2%,而后卫相撞占19.5%.
控制器在圆锥内没有可见的路由时取取出这两个更短的移动类型.
因此,长期承诺发生在航道被展望的地方,短步则发生在航道被展望的地方.
在全部前行的12.9%中,代理行走的距离小于0.23米,因为它沿着障碍滑行,而下个决定最多在1.05米后处理出一个新的框架.
在1.5米以内有甲骨文路由轴承和甲骨文站,同样承诺达到99.7%的SR(第4.3节)。

blocks.en:
Table 11 lists the quantities that describe the cost of one call independently of the GPU, in particular tokens and floating-point operations (FLOPs).
On the 1,839 unseen-building instructions in bfloat16, a decision of AlphaNav processes 241 tokens on average.
These tokens comprise 210 image-block tokens, namely 192 visual tokens with their start and end markers, and 31.4 instruction tokens, with a median of 29 and a maximum of 133.
We estimate the compute analytically as 2 × 2\times parameters × \times tokens per module.
The estimate counts 407 M vision-tower parameters over 768 image patches before the 2 × 2 2\times 2 merge and 1409 M decoder parameters over the sequence.
It yields 1.31 TFLOPs per decision on average, including 0.62 TFLOPs in the vision tower, and 1.59 TFLOPs for the longest instruction.
This estimate excludes attention over the sequence and the heads.
At the measured decision latency, this load corresponds to 3,708 tokens and an estimated 20.1 TFLOPs per second on the RTX 5070.
GA-VLN reports 8.73 theoretical TFLOPs per inference, which is 6.7 times our estimate.
The same rule applied to the 8B NaVILA, with its 1,737 context tokens and 10 generated tokens, yields 28.0 TFLOPs, which is 21.4 times our estimate.
The other papers report only frames or tokens per frame.

blocks.en:
We also test whether a short fine-tuning on pairs of camera renders improves the policy on new cameras.
Four arms fine-tune the trained policy for 1,500 steps at a learning rate of 2 × 10 − 5 2\times 10^{-5} , and every arm keeps one forward pass per decision.
The control fine-tunes on single renders, the two-view imitation arm imitates both renders of each pose, and two further arms add a Jensen-Shannon consistency term between the two route-bearing distributions, on all bins (unrestricted) or on the bins that both cameras observe (common support).
The pairs use fields of view from 70 ∘ 70^{\circ} to 100 ∘ 100^{\circ} , heights from 1.0 to 1.5 m, and pitch from − 10 ∘ -10^{\circ} to 0 ∘ 0^{\circ} .
The control and the unrestricted arm raise the SR at 120 ∘ 120^{\circ} from 14.7% to 35.7% and 33.3%, and every arm loses success at the other three cameras (Table 13 ).
AlphaNav therefore uses no camera fine-tuning.
Related methods condition on camera parameters with feature-wise linear modulation (FiLM) [ 21 ] , canonicalize geometry [ 14 ] , use spherical range images with validity masks [ 24 ] , or enforce cross-view action consistency [ 12 ] .

blocks.en:
The memory rule relies on odometry through one comparison per decision, which tests whether the agent lies at least 0.5 m from the position of the last appended frame.
Compared with appending every frame, this rule raises SR on the 300 selection episodes by + 2.7 +2.7 points at stop threshold 0.9 (62.7% against 60.0%) and from 58.7% to 62.0% at stop threshold 0.7, at the same cost per decision.
To test how sensitive the rule is to odometry errors, we replay the logged positions of the three seeds on unseen buildings.
In this replay, 52.5% of the decisions append a frame, 23.1% lie less than 0.05 m from the last appended position because of turns in place and blocked moves, and 15.8% lie between 0.4 and 0.6 m.
Scaling the measured distance by a factor between 0.9 and 1.1 leaves the outcome of the test unchanged for at least 92.3% of the logged decisions, and a factor between 0.8 and 1.2 leaves it unchanged for at least 91.2%.
An odometer that always reports motion reduces the rule to appending every frame, which is the setting measured above.
For actuation, the simulator executes turns and moves exactly except at obstacles, where 12.9% of the forward moves end short through sliding contact (Sec. S6 ).

blocks.en: S8 Failure analysis

blocks.en:
This section analyzes the failures of the policy, most of which come from the stop decision.
The stop head ranks decisions with an AUROC of 0.89, and SR on unseen buildings stays between 51.6% and 53.3% for every threshold from 0.6 to 0.9.
Over three seeds, 34.0% of the episodes stop without any decision within 3 m of the goal, and 8.9% pass within 3 m and fail (8.5% after a stop elsewhere, the others without a stop).
An oracle stop lifts seed 42 from 53.6% to 72.5% SR (Sec. 4.3 ).

The stop head receives the heatmap-pooled current-view state.
Training labels a decision as positive within a geodesic distance of 2 m from the goal and uses the measured class weight w = 4.64 w=4.64 .
At inference, we correct the logit by ln ⁡ w = 1.53 \ln w=1.53 and compare the resulting probability with 0.9 (Sec. 3.4 ).
Over the three seeds on unseen buildings, 4.2% of the episodes do not stop at all, 34.0% stop without any decision within 3 m of the goal, 8.5% stop elsewhere after a decision within 3 m, and 32.4% stop more than 5 m from the goal.
These far stops account for 69.3% of the failures.
Of all stops, 55.6% lie within 3 m and 36.4% lie within 1.5 m of the goal.

blocks.en:
Table 14 reports the calibration of the stop probability, that is, how closely the predicted probability matches the observed rate of decisions near the goal.
Over the 142,458 policy decisions, the corrected probability separates decisions within 2 m of the goal from the others with an AUROC of 0.89, or 0.86 for 3 m.
Its expected calibration error (ECE), which averages the gap between the predicted probability and the observed rate of positive labels over probability bins, is 0.076.
The probability averages 0.54 within 2 m and 0.07 beyond 5 m.
Above 0.5, the probability is overconfident.
Only 19.1% of the decisions between 0.5 and 0.6, 25.6% of those between 0.8 and 0.9, and 45.4% of the 5,284 decisions above 0.9 lie within 2 m.
These 5,284 decisions are the stops, and their probability averages 0.955.

Table 15 replays the logged episodes at lower thresholds.
At a lower threshold, an episode stops at its first decision whose corrected stop probability exceeds the new value.
Up to this decision, the logged trajectory equals the trajectory of a run at that threshold, and the replay is therefore exact.
As a check, replaying the run of the inference batch with stop threshold 0.9 at 0.8 and 0.7 reproduces the measured runs at these thresholds in 300 and 300 of their 300 episodes.
On unseen buildings, every lower threshold lowers SR, from 53.3% at 0.9 to 52.9% at 0.8 and 48.5% at 0.3.
Applying 0.9 to the uncorrected probability corresponds to a corrected threshold of 0.66 and yields 52.1% SR.
The logit correction therefore adds 1.2 points.
We fixed the threshold of 0.9 together with the memory spacing on 300 selection episodes, where it reaches 62.7% against 62.0% at 0.7 (Sec. S10 ), before the unseen-building evaluation.
On all 778 selection episodes, a threshold of 0.7 achieves the highest replayed SR (61.4% against 60.8% at 0.9), and on unseen buildings this threshold yields 52.3% ( − 0.9 -0.9 points).

The best threshold per episode reaches 61.5%.
A lower threshold can only stop earlier.
However, 34.0% of the episodes already stop before any decision within 3 m, and the oracle stop of Sec. 4.3 gains by letting these episodes continue.

blocks.en:
Finally, we test a stop-focused on-policy recipe.
This recipe uses a focal stop loss with γ = 2 \gamma=2 , which down-weights decisions that the head already classifies well, together with a larger policy share ( α = 0.85 \alpha=0.85 in Eq. 5 ) and uniform start headings in half of the rollouts.
It trains from the stage-1 checkpoint of seed 42 and uses a stop threshold of 0.4, selected on the 300 selection episodes.
The recipe halves the calibration error (0.034 against 0.070 for seed 42) and raises the AUROC from 0.89 to 0.91 at a comparable SR.
In its single evaluation on unseen buildings, the recipe reaches 53.2% SR and 50.1% SPL ( − 0.3 -0.3 [ − 2.6 -2.6 , + 2.4 +2.4 ] points against seed 42).
On all 778 selection episodes, it differs from the adopted recipe by − 1.2 -1.2 [ − 5.3 -5.3 , + 3.2 +3.2 ] points (Table 19 ).
The recipe stops beyond 5 m in 33.3% of its episodes, compared with 32.9% for seed 42.
The better-calibrated probability therefore stops far from the goal equally often.

因此,更精确的概率往往与目标相去甚远。

Because training always uses eight memory frames, keeping fewer frames at inference measures how strongly the stop decision depends on its trained input sequence.
On 300 selection episodes with seed 42 of AlphaNav, success falls from 62.7% with all eight frames to 18.0% with four frames and 0.0% with none, and without memory frames no episode stops (Table 16 ).

在有AlphaNav42种子的300个选集中,成功率从所有8个帧的62.7%下降到了18.0%,4个帧和0.0%,没有内存帧,没有插曲(表16).

blocks.en:
With one seed per model and a stop threshold of 0.6, truncating the memory during training lowers SR by 3.3 points and raises far stops from 44.5% to 49.3% of the episodes (Table 17 ).
This result suggests that the far stops depend on more than elapsed time.

We measure latency on one 12 GB RTX 5070 in bfloat16 at batch size 1.

blocks.en:
At deployment, the policy receives the instruction, the current 256 × 256 256\times 256 RGB frame, the eight memory frames, and the camera vector 𝜿 \bm{\kappa} .
This vector contains the logarithms of the focal lengths and the principal point relative to the image size, the camera height and pitch, and the robot width and turning radius.
The memory rule uses the displacement since the last appended frame, which a robot obtains from odometry.
During training, the memory holds the eight previous decision frames, without the spacing rule.
When fewer than eight frames are available, copies of the oldest frame fill the remaining slots, so the sequence length stays fixed.
The controller uses only the policy outputs, and rendered depth serves only to build the training labels.

The training logs show which terms supervise the outputs.
At every logged step of stage 1 and of the on-policy rounds, they contain five weighted terms, namely the waypoint-heatmap Kullback-Leibler (KL) divergence (1.0), the pixel L1 loss (0.5), the route-bearing cross-entropy (1.0), the visibility loss (0.25), and the stop loss (0.5).
The logged total equals their weighted sum, and the displacement and absolute-heading heads have weight zero.
The heatmap and pixel terms therefore supervise the waypoint to which the image-plane readouts of Tables 3 b and 6 steer, and the route-bearing term supervises the bearing readout.

blocks.en:
Stage 1, the initial imitation training, trains the policy with AdamW for 10,000 steps.
It samples R2R-CE training episodes, English RxR-CE training episodes, and 30,000 EnvDrop episodes with weights 0.5, 0.3, and 0.2, respectively.
All episodes are restricted to training houses [ 27 ] .
Stage 1 applies photometric jitter and randomizes the camera parameters in 25% of episodes, with fields of view between 80 ∘ 80^{\circ} and 100 ∘ 100^{\circ} (Table 20 ).
We select the checkpoint by a closed-loop evaluation on 100 Val-Seen episodes every 2,500 steps.
blocks.zh:
第1阶段,即初始模仿训练,与AdamW一起训练一万步政策.
它对R2R-CE训练节目,英语RxR-CE训练节目,以及分别有0.5分,0.3分和0.2分重量的30,000分EnvDrop节目进行了抽样.
所有节目都限于训练所[27].
第1阶段在25%的镜头中应用了光度测焦并随机分出相机参数,视域介于80~80~Circ}到100~100~100~Circ}(表20)之间.
我们每2500个步骤对100个Val-Seen事件进行闭路评估来选择检查站。

blocks.en:
On-policy correction extends the supervision to states that the policy reaches after its own errors.
We run the current policy on R2R-CE training episodes and label the visited states with the reference-route targets defined above.
Following DAgger (dataset aggregation) [ 25 ] , we aggregate these corrections with the original data and sample half of each batch from them.
The probability that the policy controls decision i i follows the Efficient-VLN schedule [ 41 ] : P policy ​ ( i ) = α p i , p i = min ⁡ ( 1 , i / ( L − 1 ) ) , α = 0.6 . P_{\mathrm{policy}}(i)=\alpha^{\,p_{i}},\qquad p_{i}=\min\!\big(1,\ i/(L-1)\big),\quad\alpha=0.6. (5) Here, L L denotes the expected number of decisions.
The probability of policy control is therefore close to 1 early in the episode and falls to 0.6 at its expected end.
If the agent is more than 1 m from the reference path or is blocked by an obstacle after a policy decision, the oracle takes control for five decisions.
Control then returns to the policy.
With these takeovers, the policy drives 65.0% of the rollout steps, which is the on-policy share of this schedule.
The ablation of Table 3 a compares it with a round-level schedule, in which the oracle acts with probability 0.5 r + 1 0.5^{r+1} at the start of round r r , a probability that then rises toward the end of the episode.
This schedule collects 1,000 rollouts per round, uses the same takeovers, and lets the policy drive 47.3% of the rollout steps.
We run three correction rounds, each with 1,500 rollouts followed by 1,200 fine-tuning steps at a learning rate of 5 × 10 − 5 5\times 10^{-5} .
Both augmentations stay active during correction.

blocks.en:
Stage 1 draws on 10,352 R2R-CE episodes with 162,493 records, 18,490 English RxR-CE episodes with 421,164 records, and 28,671 EnvDrop episodes with 502,544 records.
In total, it uses 57,513 episodes and 1,086,201 records.
Before the expert follower generates the trajectories, we remove the RxR-CE and EnvDrop episodes whose start and goal both lie within 0.5 m of those of an evaluation or selection route.
This filter removes 15 and 32 episodes, respectively.
The expert follower completes the episodes counted above within its decision limit, out of 10,819 R2R-CE, 19,981 RxR-CE, and 30,000 sampled EnvDrop episodes.
We use the R2R-CE training split as released, and its six episodes on two routes within 0.5 m of a selection route lie outside the generated set.
The baseline recipe of Table 3 c trains on the R2R-CE part alone for 4,000 steps without the two augmentations.

第1阶段借鉴了10,352个R2R-CE集,收录了162,493个记录,18,490个英语RxR-CE集收录了421,164个记录,28,671个EnvDrop集收录了502,544个记录.
它总共使用了57,513集和1,086,201个记录.
在专家追随者产生出出轨迹之前,我们删除了RxR-CE和EnvDrop的相片,其起步和目标均在评价或选择路线的相片的0.5米以内.
此过滤器分别删除了15集和32集.
专家追随者在决定限度内完成以上所统计的相片,在10,819个R2R-CE,19,981个RxR-CE,30,000个抽样EnvDrop相片.
我们使用R2R-CE的分解训练作为发布,它在选择路线0.5米以内的两条路线上的六集位于生成的集合之外.
仅R2R-CE部分的表3c列车的基线配方,用于4000个步骤而无需两个扩能.
